content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Identify and use the fact that angles on a straight line sum to $180°$
Identify and use the fact that angles at a point sum to $360°$
Recognise and use the property that vertically opposite angles are equal
Apply multiple angle facts together to solve multi-step problems
Give clear geometric reasons for each step of a calculation

Angles are everywhere in the real world -- from the hands of a clock to the pitch of a roof, from the opening of a door to the design of a bridge. Understanding angle facts is the foundation of all geometry. These rules allow us to find unknown angles without needing to measure them, using logical reasoning instead.
In examinations, you will frequently be asked to find missing angles and
for each step. Learning to do this precisely is a key skill.
Before we explore angle facts, let's review the types of angles:
Between a right angle and a straight line
Key Concept 1: Angles on a Straight Line
Angles on a straight line sum to $180°$.
When two or more angles are formed on one side of a straight line at a single point, their total is always $180°$.
If there are more than two angles:
A straight line represents a half turn, and a half turn is $180°$.
Key Concept 2: Angles at a Point
Angles at a point sum to $360°$.
When several angles meet at a single point and together form a full turn, their total is always $360°$.
A full turn around a point is $360°$.
When two straight lines cross, they form two pairs of equal angles. The angles that are across from each other (not adjacent) are called
If two lines intersect, forming angles $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ going around the point:
Consider angles $a$ and $b$ on a straight line: $a + b = 180°$. Also $b + c = 180°$ (on the other straight line). Therefore $a = c$.
Example 1: Angles on a Straight Line
Two angles on a straight line are $x$ and $125°$. Find $x$.

$$\begin{aligned}
x + 125° &= 180° \quad \text{(angles on a straight line)} \\
x &= 180° - 125° \\
x &= 55°
\end{aligned}$$
Example 2: Three Angles on a Straight Line
Three angles on a straight line are $42°$, $x$, and $68°$. Find $x$.

$$\begin{aligned}
42° + x + 68° &= 180° \quad \text{(angles on a straight line)} \\
x + 110° &= 180° \\
x &= 180° - 110° \\
x &= 70°
\end{aligned}$$
Four angles meet at a point. Three of them are $110°$, $85°$, and $95°$. Find the fourth angle.

$$\begin{aligned}
110° + 85° + 95° + x &= 360° \quad \text{(angles at a point)} \\
290° + x &= 360° \\
x &= 360° - 290° \\
x &= 70°
\end{aligned}$$
Example 4: Vertically Opposite Angles and Multi-Step
Two straight lines intersect. One of the angles formed is $3x + 10°$ and the vertically opposite angle is $70°$. Find $x$.
Two straight lines cross. One angle is $y$, and the angle adjacent to it is $2y + 30°$. Find $y$.
Adjacent angles on a straight line sum to $180°$:

$$\begin{aligned}
y + (2y + 30°) &= 180° \quad \text{(angles on a straight line)} \\
3y + 30° &= 180° \\
3y &= 150° \\
y &= 50°
\end{aligned}$$
We can verify: the four angles at the point are $50°$, $130°$, $50°$, $130°$, which sum to $360°$. ✓
Assuming angles on a straight line sum to $360°$
$360°$ is a full turn; a straight line is a half turn
Angles on a straight line sum to $180°$
Confusing adjacent angles with vertically opposite angles
Adjacent angles are next to each other; vertically opposite are across from each other
Vertically opposite angles are the ones that do NOT share a side
Forgetting to state the geometric reason
Exam mark schemes require a reason for each step
Always write the angle fact used, e.g. "angles on a straight line"
Angles must be given in degrees (or radians at higher level)
Two angles on a straight line are $x$ and $140°$. Find $x$.
Three angles on a straight line are $55°$, $x$, and $85°$. Find $x$.
Two angles at a point are $x$ and $290°$. Find $x$.
Four angles at a point are $90°$, $120°$, $x$, and $80°$. Find $x$.
Two straight lines intersect. One angle is $65°$. Find the other three angles.
Angles on a straight line are $x$, $2x$, and $3x$. Find the value of $x$.
Two straight lines cross. The angles formed are $3a + 10°$, $b$, $70°$, and $b$. Find $a$ and $b$.
Three straight lines meet at a point. The six angles formed, going around the point, are: $x$, $2x$, $x$, $2x$, $x$, $2x$. Find $x$.
Two angles on a straight line are $(5x - 20)°$ and $(3x + 8)°$. Find the size of each angle.
Two lines intersect. One angle is $(4y + 5)°$ and an adjacent angle is $(6y - 15)°$. Find $y$ and state the size of all four angles.
At a point, four angles are $(2x + 10)°$, $(3x - 20)°$, $(x + 50)°$, and $(4x)°$. Find $x$ and each angle.
Prove that vertically opposite angles are equal, using the fact that angles on a straight line sum to $180°$.
The vertically opposite angle is $65°$. The two adjacent angles are each $180° - 65° = 115°$. The four angles are $65°$, $115°$, $65°$, $115°$.
Vertically opposite: $3a + 10° = 70°$, so $3a = 60°$, giving $a = 20°$. Adjacent: $b + 70° = 180°$, so $b = 110°$.

Adjacent angles on a straight line: $(4y + 5) + (6y - 15) = 180$, so $10y - 10 = 180$, giving $10y = 190$, $y = 19$. One pair: $4(19) + 5 = 81°$. Other pair: $6(19) - 15 = 99°$. The four angles are $81°$, $99°$, $81°$, $99°$.
Let the two lines form angles $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ in order. On one line: $a + b = 180°$. On the other line: $b + c = 180°$. Therefore $a + b = b + c$, which gives $a = c$. Similarly $b = d$.

Use precise geometric language: say "angles on a straight line" not "they add up to 180".
Check your answer makes sense -- an angle on a straight line cannot be more than $180°$.
If angles meet at a point, check they sum to $360°$ as a verification.
Always state the geometric reason for each step in a calculation
These angle facts are the building blocks for more advanced geometry
